[package]
name = "link-assistant-router"
version = "1.24.1"
edition = "2024"
description = "Link.Assistant.Router — Claude MAX OAuth proxy and token gateway for Anthropic APIs"
readme = "../README.md"
license = "Unlicense"
keywords = ["proxy", "anthropic", "claude", "gateway", "oauth"]
categories = ["web-programming::http-server"]
repository = "https://github.com/link-assistant/router"
documentation = "https://docs.rs/link-assistant-router"
rust-version = "1.89"
exclude = ["dev/log/**"]

[lib]
name = "link_assistant_router"
path = "src/lib.rs"

# The canonical command is `router`: the name the project, its repository and
# its documentation already use for itself (issue #222). The original name is
# kept as a second binary from the same source so existing scripts, deployments
# and documented commands keep working. That target has its own file, which
# `include!`s `src/main.rs`: Cargo warns on every build when two targets name
# the same file (issue #648).
[[bin]]
name = "router"
path = "src/main.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "link-assistant-router"
path = "src/bin/link-assistant-router.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "with-router"
path = "src/bin/with-router.rs"

[dependencies]
axum = { version = "0.8", features = ["macros", "ws"] }
hyper = { version = "1.11", features = ["full"] }
hyper-util = { version = "0.1", features = ["tokio"] }
reqwest = { version = "0.13", features = ["stream", "json", "form", "query", "cookies", "socks"] }
cookie_store = "0.22.1"
url = "2.5"
tokio = { version = "1.53", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "time", "signal", "fs", "process", "sync", "net"] }
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
schemars = { version = "1.2", features = ["chrono04"] }
jsonschema = { version = "0.58", default-features = false }
serde_json = "1.0"
toml_edit = "0.25"
jsonwebtoken = { version = "11.0", default-features = false, features = ["rust_crypto"] }
chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }
uuid = { version = "1.26", features = ["v4"] }
getrandom = "0.4"
tower = { version = "0.5", features = ["util"] }
tower-http = { version = "0.7", features = ["trace", "cors"] }
tracing = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter", "json"] }
log-lazy = "0.2"
bytes = "1.12"
futures-util = "0.3"
tokio-tungstenite = { version = "0.30", features = ["rustls-tls-webpki-roots"] }
http = "1.5"
http-body-util = "0.1"
lino-arguments = "0.3"
lino-objects-codec = "0.7.0"
links-notation = "0.22.0"
doublets = "0.5.0"
link-cli = "0.2.10"
clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive", "env", "string"] }
base64 = "0.23"
async-trait = "0.1"
sha2 = "0.11"
hex = "0.4"
aes-gcm = "0.11"
portable-pty = "0.9"
os_info = "3.15.0"
rust-embed = { version = "8.12.0", default-features = false }
tempfile = "3"
axum-server = { version = "0.8.0", features = ["tls-rustls"] }
rcgen = "0.14.9"
flate2 = "1.1.10"
brotli = "9.0.0"
zstd = "0.14.0"
fs2 = "0.4"
reflink-copy = "0.1.30"
vt100 = "0.16"

[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
process-wrap = { version = "10.0.1", default-features = false, features = ["std", "job-object"] }

[dev-dependencies]
proptest = "1"
tokio-test = "0.4"
tower = { version = "0.5", features = ["util"] }
wait-timeout = "0.2"
criterion = { version = "0.8", default-features = false, features = ["cargo_bench_support"] }

# This is an importing application, run as its own process rather than a
# libtest harness. It rejects Router CLI arguments to detect wrong launches.
[[example]]
name = "host_library_consumer"
test = true
harness = false

# Hot-path benchmarks (issue #672); the Benchmarks workflow compares a pull
# request against its base with scripts/compare-benchmarks.rs.
[[bench]]
name = "hot_paths"
harness = false

[lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"

[lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
nursery = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
# These handlers return an axum `Response` as their error, which is the whole
# point: a rejected request answers the caller directly rather than bubbling a
# code the caller would have to translate. `Response` is large, so the lint
# fires on every one of them; boxing it would add an allocation and a deref to
# a path that is already returning by value. Raised to a warning by Rust
# 1.98's clippy, which this branch is the first to run.
result_large_err = "allow"

# Allow some common patterns
module_name_repetitions = "allow"
too_many_lines = "allow"
missing_errors_doc = "allow"
missing_panics_doc = "allow"

[package.metadata.cargo-semver-checks.lints]
enum_variant_added = { level = "allow" }
# Issues #722/#724 extend public defaultable configuration/context structs.
# Keep this lint enabled, requiring a minor release for reviewed field additions.
constructible_struct_adds_field = { required-update = "minor" }

# This file is automatically @generated by Cargo.
# It is not intended for manual editing.
version = 4

# Fixed-integer arithmetic contracts

These adapters are independently implemented from the pinned Rust 1.89 primitive
arithmetic and Ord contracts. No Rust source function is substituted, and no Rust
compiler or executable was used. Exact source hashes and primary URLs appear in
../fixtures/rust-fixed-integer-sources.json.

The factory specializes only an actual checked fixed integer. Checked results
use registered standard Option provenance. Ordinary Ord methods remain distinct
from const-eligible arithmetic. Typed domain failure is distinct from the source
clamp panic; neither becomes a fabricated successful result.

The implementation excludes floating point, mixed signed operands, unregistered wrapping operations and
unchecked arithmetic, division, clocks, arbitrary trait implementations and
alternate pointer-width profiles. Frontend instantiation and dependency checking
are required before any original caller becomes executable. Runtime parity
remains false.

The separate source-only fixed-wrapping draft adds only `wrapping_add/sub` for
actual checked signed/unsigned fixed primitives through128bits. The original
primitive `Self`/width invocation, complete macro member and generic modulo
intrinsic are retained in `source-profiles/fixed-wrapping/`; the new authored
cases are unrun. This is not whole-macro expansion, whole-core or formatter
authority. Pointer profiles, mixed operands and custom numeric owners refuse.
The existing source receipt describes the earlier checked/saturating/Ord scope.

The fixed integer adapters were independently implemented in JavaScript from
the public parsing contracts and inspected Rust 1.89.0 core numeric source.
They preserve checked digit/overflow ordering and the pinned ParseIntError
categories and Display strings. They do not copy a Router function body.

The checked JSON adapters implement contracts inspected in the local source of
serde_json 1.0.151, as pinned by this repository's Cargo.lock, and its formatter
dependency zmij 1.0.23. No Rust executable was used to validate these adapters.

The byte decoder and default numeric accumulator in json-parser.mjs and
json-numbers.mjs adapt algorithms from serde_json src/de.rs and src/read.rs.
serde_json is copyright its contributors and distributed under MIT OR Apache-2.0.
This copy uses the MIT license reproduced in json-LICENSE-MIT.txt.

The shortest binary64 decimal selector uses independent BigInt rational
arithmetic. Its notation thresholds follow the inspected zmij 1.0.23 f64
formatter: fixed exponents -5 through 15, signed scientific exponents, and an
explicit decimal fraction for integral floats. No zmij implementation is copied.

Source hashes, selected contract references, feature assumptions and validation
limits are recorded in ../fixtures/rust-json-sources.json. In particular, these
fixtures do not establish differential equivalence against every Rust float,
every malformed input or a complete Router program. Mutable Value borrows and
arbitrary derived serde types require their own frontend checking.

The runtime draft executes the original serde_json1.0.151 f64 lexical branch
structure on at most768 raw mantissa digits. The exact original cached_float80
source is retained as licensed data with SHA-256 verification. The package
archive, full23 original source members and licenses are independently pinned
by the portable source profile. Bundled MIT/Apache texts apply to source data.

Fast/moderate acceptance, upper-product rounding, normalization, error counters,
downward candidate, half-way comparison and positive hi64/sticky native rounding
are preserved rather than replaced by ideal rounding. The reusable mantissa
operation deliberately retains the source's unconditional sticky injection for
larger integer tails; the JSON reader still refuses those inputs as an explicit
unsupported domain. The769-digit discrepancy is SOURCE-INFERRED, not measured
with Rust. Existing default JSON numeric parsing and its guard are unchanged.

These direct-branch cases are UNRUN. Branch fidelity, bounded limb arithmetic,
source feature-directed admission and source identity remain review/test
obligations. Runtime/native parity and complete allocation/OOM/drop/application
effects are not asserted. Arithmetic uses the declared ordinary IEEE binary64
nearest-even environment and successful resource assumptions.

These generic pure time adapters use the semantic contracts of Rust 1.89.0 `std::time::Duration`, implemented in the official [core/time.rs](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.89.0/library/core/src/time.rs). Rust is licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0. This repository implements the contracts independently; it does not replace individual Router Rust functions with handwritten JavaScript.

The downloaded source SHA256, byte count, function const markers and Router lexical usage inventory are recorded in `../fixtures/time-contract-provenance.json`. The source was inspected without running Rust. The algebraic record is a lowering representation of exact u64 seconds and normalized u32 nanoseconds, not a claim about physical Rust memory layout or permission to access private Rust fields.

Duration `min`/`max` use the pinned [core/cmp.rs](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.89.0/library/core/src/cmp.rs) default `Ord` methods and the derived seconds-then-nanoseconds ordering. Equal operands select the first operand for `min` and the second for `max`, retaining the checked immutable Copy operand. Both methods are pure and non-const in the pinned profile.

`time-contracts.mjs` registers stable pure method/type signatures, immutable Option/Result layouts, explicit `pure: true` and source-grounded `constEligible` metadata. Trait arithmetic, comparisons, `Default`, floating constructors and float-error string conversion are pure but not const in this pinned profile. ZERO/MAX constants are registered separately. The registry must preserve these distinctions instead of treating deterministic host calls as automatically const or allowing arbitrary source-private constructors.

`time-runtime.mjs` uses BigInt for fixed integers, throws on malformed checked values or source panic paths, and returns real typed Option/Result outcomes. Floating construction decodes the original IEEE-754 binary64 rational and rounds to nanoseconds with ties to even; it does not multiply a rounded JavaScript Number by a billion first. There is no clock, timer, filesystem, network or environment capability in the runtime.

Independent fixtures exercise the semantic checker layouts, u64/u32/u128 boundaries, borrow/carry, underflow, division remainder, saturation, source panic distinctions, immutable owner fields, binary64 ties, nanosecond carry, finite-domain errors and const metadata. These prove the adapter subset in Node/Bun, not whole Router execution. The frontend registry and generated-code integration are separate obligations. f32, unstable unit constructors, clocks, sleep, chrono, debug formatting, iterator Sum and assignment/borrow semantics remain explicit limitations.
